2: OIL INDUSTRY SAFETY DIRECTORATE. EDS: OISD: ACCI/06, Dt: 14.02.2022. Sub: INVESTIGATION COMMITTEE REPORT ON FIRE INCIDENT AT IOCL-HALDIA REFINERY ON 21.12.2021. 1.0 INTRODUCTION: MSQ units were under planned shutdown since 13.12.2021 and various shutdown jobs were being carried out after normal shutdown and hand over of the units to Maintenance. Indian Oil Corporation Limited, Haldia Refinery (IOCL-HR) informed that at around 14:50 hrs on 21st December 2021, a fire had occurred in the area of MSQ Block (Isomerization) of the Refinery while grating/structure cutting job was being carried out in the first platform of Stabilizer area. The fire was put-off by applying water by personnel working in the vicinity and subsequently by Firefighting crew. The duration of the fire was less than 15 minutes as per FIR copy. There were 3 fatalities and 44 injuries of contract personnel due to the incident as reported in the FIR. However, IOCL subsequently revised the casualty figure to 3 fatalities and 41 injuries. At the time of release of this report, total fatalities increased to 5. There was no injury to any of the IOCL personnel. 1.1 Committee comprising: Shri Udit Nandi (CGM Safety, HPCL-Visakh Refinery), Shri S Giridharan (GM Maint, BPCL-Kochi Refinery), Shri Jamunalal Rout (Dy. Director, PNGRB), Shri Harendra Kumar Yadav (Addl. Director P&E, OISD). Terms of reference: Investigate the incident, identify lapses and root cause(s), recommend corrective action to avoid recurrence.
3: 2.0 INVESTIGATION MODALITIES: Committee visited incident site from 23rd to 24th December 2021. Visits to MSQ plant, field room, main control room of MSQ block, fire station. Interacted with stakeholders including CGM TS&HSE A Sanyal, CGM T D Dutta, DGM HSE Daniel Raj, AMPS Shubham Jain, ITM Mridul Deka, CMFS Ashok Kumar Raghuvanshi, SPNE Panner Selvam Ponnusamy, SPNE Golap Thakuria, SPNE Amit Binwal, AMPN Shahrukh Husain Ansari, DGM PN K.S. Paul, SMFS S.M. Raut, SMNM Jaydip Chattaraj, AMFS Sreekuttan M.S, SF&SO Neelabh Gupta, SPNM Saurabh Mukherjee, MNMEL Samaresh Biswas, AM Mulakala Venkata Niranjan, AM-ML Himagna Sen.
4: Interaction with personnel continued: SIPM Naveen Kumar, Field Operators Mukesh, Ankit Chaturvedi, Susanta Das, Kanak Kanti Sahoo, Krishnanand Kharwal, Saroj Dey, Rangan Datta, Ranjit Pratap Singh, Devendra Dhar Dwivedi, MD Mahasin Khan, Rajib Kuiti, Sanjoy Mandal, Daruknath Mandal, Dipanjan Mal. Shilpi contractors: Sanjay Sahai, Konshik Gole, Zanaklal, Rishin Raj. Injured personnel could not be contacted as all were under treatment at Kolkata. Review of documents: DCS logbooks, field logbooks, maintenance register, work permits, registers in control room, SOPs, CCTV footage DHDS-508, DHDS-509, DHDS-510, DHDS-701, DHDS-515. Review of IOCL internal investigation findings.
5: 3.0 BACKGROUND: Haldia Refinery situated on banks of river Hoogly, Haldia, West Bengal, crude processing capacity 8.0 MMTPA. Commissioned in 1975. MSQ block comprises VDU-II, Prime-G, Isomerization (Unit 86) and NHT (Unit 85). Manning of MSQ units on day of incident: Field operators (JEA): normal 4, actual on 21.12.2021: 7; Panel: 1; Shift In-charge (SIC): normal 1, actual 2; Contract personnel: approx. 340. Two Production officers deployed in shift; Single SIC not designated. 4.0 INCIDENT DESCRIPTION AND CHRONOLOGY OF EVENTS: MSQ block units planned shutdown: NHT 24 days, ISOM 24 days, Prime-G 52 days, VDU-2 4 days. Isomerization unit shutdown activities ongoing since 13.12.2021. a. ISOM unit (including Stabilizer column, 86-C-01 circuits) made hydrocarbon free by N2 purging, water flushing and steam purging.
6: b. Stabilizer column (86-C-01) blinded on 20.12.2021. On 21.12.2021, stabilizer reboiler (86-E-06) inlet flanges were being opened to facilitate blinding for hydrotest of reboiler inlet circuit as one of shutdown jobs. c. During flange opening activity of Reboiler inlet line, Naphtha along with water started coming out through opening. d. At 14:50 hrs, explosion followed by fire on first floor of Unit 86 (ISOM) at Stabilizer column area; fire continued for less than 15 minutes. Fire call received from MCP 609 and simultaneously message on walkie-talkie regarding fire in MSQ unit. e. Initial fire fighting started with water spray from nearby ground monitors and fire hydrants by contractor personnel. Fire tender-1 from main fire station and Fire tender-4 from satellite fire station responded. f. Rescue operation started, casualties shifted to Occupational Health Centre and Kolkata hospitals. g. Shutdown manpower from surrounding areas evacuated and affected area cordoned off. Fig 1 shows site activities: Naphtha leaked from flange opening and gas cutting job at 3 m away from flange for 86-B-13 vessel structure cutting location.
7: 5.0 Scene of Accident as noted during investigation team visit to site: 1) At site visit, no activities going on as PESO had given order not to carry out job in unit. 2) CISF cordoned off unit. 3) Stabilizer column (86-C-01) shell flanges including reboiler inlet and outlet lines were noted in blinded condition. 4) Considerable material damage at incident site. Anchoring hooks of safety belt of deceased along with tools and tackles (wrench, spanner, hammer) were found present at site. Tools and tackles were found to be of normal metallic design (i.e. not of 'Non sparking' type). 6.0 Observations by investigation committee: 6.1 DCS trends: 1) Isomerization unit feed reduced at 22:00 hrs on 12.12.2021 and cut out done at 00:00 hrs on 13.12.2021. 2) Steaming of Stabilizer column (86-C-01) carried out from 15.12.2021 to 17.12.2021. 3) Column 86-C-01 bottom level remained low between 13.12.2021 and 19.12.2021 (4-5%). On 19.12.2021 level increased to 104% at 13:50 hrs and came down to 0% at 16:35 hrs.
8: 4) Reboiler 86-E-06 inlet temperature reached maximum of 81°C on 17.12.2021 during steam purging phase. Inferred that reboiler circuit did not get steam purged adequately. 5) Difference in timing (varying between days/minutes) amongst time record of DCS clock, CCTV footages, alarm server time. 6) On 24.12.2021, in presence of investigating team and IOCL internal team, water poured in reboiler vapor return line by opening thermo-well flange (86TI0604). Naphtha observed coming out from reboiler inlet flanges at bottom (which were in open condition). Sample sent to laboratory: confirmed Light Naphtha properties (IBP 52°C / FBP 75°C). Reboiler and stabilizer column common drain line was found choked. Naphtha was still remaining inside the reboiler vessel/circuit although steaming/N2 purging activities had been done as per shutdown procedure.
9: 7) HC gas detector 82006AI0301A activated for high-high alarm at 13:10:27 hrs on 21.12.2021 (prior to 14:50 fire). IOCL should ensure all critical alarms are given due attention and necessary actions/checking of root cause addressed. 8) CCTV camera DHDS-515 record not available after 14:00 hrs due to non-availability of power; contradiction regarding UPS outage handover. 9) No historical trend available for HC detectors in DCS system. 6.2 Observations based on interaction with personnel: 1) 14:00 hrs was operator shift change-over time. Seven field operators deployed per shift in MSQ plant. 2) Mock drill conducted from 11:00 to 14:15 hrs in SRU, delaying vehicle entry and evening shift operators. Morning shift operators left plant prior to arrival of relievers and one operator who stayed went for lunch at time of incident. No field operators were available in ISOM Unit (Unit 86) to supervise maintenance activities. Crucial administrative gap.
10: 3) IOCL personnel were not present in unit no. 86 for supervision of maintenance jobs being carried out by contractor personnel. Regular supervision could have stopped maintenance activities (including hot job) and evacuated manpower immediately on observing Naphtha leakage. 4) Documentary evidence regarding head count of MSQ block could not be furnished. 5) Previous fire incidents / near misses prior to accident: a) Fire incident on 15.12.2021 during cutting of 2-inch LPG reprocessing line in FCC unit due to trapped hydrocarbon from improper flushing. b) Fire call on 19.12.2021 at 09:13 hrs and 17:13 hrs in culvert between MSQ and FCCU. c) On 20.12.2021, F&S officer noticed naphtha dripping from blinded flange of process line from 86-C-03 column, stopped by bolt tightening. Unsafe acts and unsafe conditions should be analysed critically. 6) Daily clearance in work permits given manually without maintaining record of list of clearances issued.
11: Work permit 9040CL21075294 for flange opening of stabilizer reboiler: production engineers stated in contradiction, file burned in incident. 7) Witnesses and CCTV footage of DHDS-508 confirmed explosion followed by fire. Intensity felt even at 100 m away. 8) Incident control room not activated subsequent to emergency; IOCL stated fire was less than 15 minutes, but explosion followed by fire in unit area is categorized as Level-2 disaster scenario under ERDMP. 6.3 Additional observations: 1) Chlorine guard bed (86-B-13) grating, adjacent to incident area, was being cut for removal from Isomerization unit; activity in progress when parallel job of blinding Stabilizer Reboiler bottom was started on 21.12.2021. 2) Refinery could not produce approval of statutory authority (PESO) for removal of chlorine guard. 3) MSQ block units not meeting inter-distance requirement of OISD-STD-118 Table-1; layout violation.
12: 4) ISOM unit observed congested with scaffolding without proper escape routes for large numbers of contract workmen (approx 340 deployed). Operation, Maintenance and Fire & Safety team should have carried out Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) for high manpower and staggered deployment. 5) Level-III mock drill in morning stopped jobs for 3 hrs, causing clustering of people in second shift to finish scheduled jobs. 6) On 23.12.2021 hot job in VDU-2 was going on without proper welding booth and personnel not wearing boiler suit/apron. 7) Overhead AFCs (86EA01, 86EA 02 A/B) have not been provided with water sprinkler system per OISD-STD-116 clause 4.2.5. 8) Neither Shift-in-charge nor Operators signed log sheet. 9) 50% of injured workers in their twenties (lowest age 19 yrs); two safety supervisors for 340 contract personnel appeared low. 10) No job specific PPEs mentioned in work order.
13: 7.0 PROBABLE REASONS OF FAILURE / ROOT CAUSE: 1) Inadequate flushing of the Reboiler circuit and lack of site supervision by IOCL during execution of non-routine activities were primary cause of incident. Final checking for ensuring 'nil' hydrocarbon presence at reboiler bottom was not carried out properly. Common drain line choked. 2) Inadequate risk awareness / sensitization among contract workmen and IOCL employees contributed to incident. As soon as Naphtha started spilling out from reboiler bottom flange, concerned personnel could have alerted all people in vicinity (particularly grating cutting job of chlorine guard vessel). 3) Due diligence w.r.t. suitable action against early sign / unsafe condition was not displayed after noticing Naphtha leak from 86-C-01 feed inlet blinding shell flange on 20th December 2021 at 10:30 hrs.
14: 8.0 CONCLUSION: 1) Based on observations, source of fuel for the fire was spilled out residual Naphtha present in reboiler (86-E-06) and connected piping during opening of reboiler inlet flanges while carrying out blinding activity. 2) Source of ignition was (a) hot job in vicinity (gas cutting job of grating for removal of chlorine guard 86-B-8) or (b) spark generated due to use of normal metallic tools. 9.0 RECOMMENDATIONS: 1. Adequacy of Standard Operating Procedure (SOPs) for flushing to be reviewed to ensure equipment-wise flushing plan and physical checking/verification to confirm system is hydrocarbon free. 2. Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) shall be conducted by Operation, Maintenance and Fire & Safety team before start of non-routine activities. 3. Maintenance crew engaged for shutdown to be made aware through supervisory control, tool box talks about potential job hazards, dos & don'ts in case of abnormal condition like oil/gas leakage. 4. Deployment of skilled manpower suitable for respective job; ensure only qualified workmen enter refinery. 5. Mandatory fire retardant / flame resistant coverall PPE policy in line with OISD-STD-155. 6. OWS and CBD drain lines of equipment to be always maintained de-choked.
15: 9.0 RECOMMENDATIONS (Continued): 7. Sufficient number of Safety supervisors shall be ensured all the time during shutdown/start-up activities with fire watch assistance. 8. A multidisciplinary team (MDT) should be constituted to carry out surprise checks during shutdown activities, to identify unsafe acts and unsafe conditions. 9. Availability of CCTV cameras at all units; use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) equipped CCTV system to be explored for auto-orientation towards abnormality/fire. 10. Portable CCTV cameras and HC Gas monitoring system (GMS) to cover critical maintenance activities. 11. Date/time difference between alarm server, DCS, CCTVs to be rectified (GPS time synchronization). 12. Man-to-man relieving in unit for proper handover and takeover of duties. 13. Logging and countersigning of daily activities in log book. 14. Scaffolding erection review for easy access and escape route; regulate simultaneous activities. 15. Prior approval of statutory authority (PESO) for layout change. 16. Simultaneous shutdown philosophy for closely spaced MSQ block units. 17. Configure all detectors (hydrocarbon, toxic) in history trend of DCS. 18. Incident control center activation as per ERDMP.
16: 19. Water sprinkler system on all Air Fin Coolers (AFCs) in hydrocarbon service per OISD-STD-116 clause 4.2.5. 20. Address observations of IOCL Internal Investigation, PESO, other investigating authorities.
